answer.label: Not securely Arthur C. Clarke — known as Amara’s law
answer.sourceLine: This formulation is known as Amara’s law. Quote Investigator traces a wider family of sayings and finds that Clarke’s documented 1951 observation does not make this same short-run/long-run distinction.

author.heading: About Roy Amara
author.bio: Roy Amara was an American futurist associated with the Institute for the Future. His name is attached to the short-run/long-run technology maxim, although related formulations have a broader history.

sourcesVerified.claim: QI documents an anonymous maxim quoted by J. C. R. Licklider in 1965, Roy Amara’s later formulations, and later Clarke attributions. It does not establish Clarke as the originator of this exact sentence. The Roy Amara biography reproduces the displayed formulation as Amara’s law; its claimed 1978 dating is not independently adopted here.
